features.title: Path normalization
features.description: server_auth::normalize_path over httplib req.path (which is ALREADY single percent-decoded by httplib at parse time, see httplib.cpp:7591). Do NOT decode again and do NOT repair the path. Strip api_prefix (return NORM_UNMATCHED if outside prefix); REJECT (NORM_REJECT->400) any NUL byte, literal '%', backslash, empty segment (double slash), trailing slash (except root), or whole '.'/'..' segment. No slash-collapsing, no trailing-slash-stripping (B1: prevents desync with httplib's PathParamsMatcher which would dispatch POST /slots/ to the ADMIN_STATE /slots/:id_slot handler). Case-sensitive. See docs/design/pr1-rbac-core.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria: //slots and /slots/ are REJECTED with HTTP 400 (B1: not silently normalized), so httplib never dispatches the ADMIN_STATE slot handler under a path authz classified differently
/Slots does not reach the /slots handler; with auth enabled an anonymous request to it is denied (B2), not allowed
/v1/%2e%2e/slots (-> /v1/../slots) and /slots%00 (-> NUL) are rejected with HTTP 400
a request whose path lacks the configured api_prefix returns NORM_UNMATCHED and is subject to deny-by-default when auth is enabled (B2)
an encoded slash %2f decodes (via httplib) to a real separator: /slots%2f0 -> /slots/0 is matched; /slots%2f -> /slots/ is rejected (trailing slash)
double-encoded sequences leave a literal '%' after httplib's single decode and are rejected, not decoded a second time
normalization is exercised by black-box HTTP tests (with a key configured) before the middleware is finalized
features.notes: Tests written FIRST (PLAN.md 4.2a). Corrections vs PLAN 4.2a: httplib pre-decodes once (no second decode); and BLOCKER B1 - reject non-canonical paths (double/trailing slash) instead of repairing them, to stay in lockstep with httplib routing.

features.title: Permission model and policy types
features.description: server_perm bitmask (PERM_PUBLIC sentinel + INFER/READ_STATE/METRICS/ADMIN_STATE/ADMIN_MODELS/PROXY), server_auth_principal, and server_auth::init loading policy from --auth-policy-file JSON with a compiled-in default. Roles are named permission sets; api_keys map SHA-256(key) hex -> role; default_role null = deny. Keys hashed with a VENDORED public-domain SHA-256 (works on all builds, no OpenSSL gate); hashed-digest lookup via unordered_map. Three modes: auth-disabled (no policy, no keys), legacy super-user (no policy, keys=PERM_ALL), RBAC (policy present). Adds only --auth-policy-file. See docs/design/pr1-rbac-core.md sections 3,4,8,10.
acceptance_criteria: policy file parse error, unknown permission name, or a key mapped to a nonexistent role aborts server startup (fail closed)
in RBAC mode, a --api-key whose hash is absent from policy.api_keys aborts startup (Q2: policy is the single source of truth, no silent default_role assignment)
at runtime, a presented key whose hash is unknown and default_role is null is rejected 401 (no default role, no permissive fallback)
roles and key->role assignments are data (policy JSON), not code: adding a role requires no C++ change
with no --auth-policy-file and no --api-key, the server behaves exactly as today (open); with no policy and an --api-key set, a valid key grants full access (legacy)

key hashing uses a vendored SHA-256 and works identically on SSL and non-SSL builds; hashed-digest comparison is a plain unordered_map lookup (C2); consttime_equal retained only for any optional raw-key legacy path
features.notes: Challenger Q1 (vendor SHA-256, no SSL gate), Q2 (--api-key absent from policy = startup error), and C2 (unordered_map lookup for hashed keys) applied.
features.done_summary: PR1 verified: build clean; path-normalization 31/31, security regression 30/30, RBAC blocker regression 1/1; curl matrix incl RBAC admin/user differentiation and B1 bypasses all pass.

features.title: Route -> permission table with startup assertion
features.description: Static (method, pattern, perm) table in server-auth.cpp covering every route registered in server.cpp:233-356, matched against normalized concrete paths with ':' segments as single-segment wildcards (mirrors httplib PathParamsMatcher). server_auth::register_route adds env-derived gcp compat paths; server_auth::is_infer_only guards the gcp /predict internal dispatch (S1). METHOD-AWARE startup assertion (S2): a new registered_routes (method,path) vector on server_http_context is populated at get/post/del and assert_routes_covered checks exact (method,pattern) coverage, aborting startup on any gap. Table lives in server-auth.cpp (not server.cpp) per the logic-in-new-files rule; the assertion is the coupling. See docs/design/pr1-rbac-core.md section 6.
acceptance_criteria: a (method,path) registered in server.cpp with no exact (method,pattern) table entry aborts startup with a clear SRV_ERR naming method and path (S2: method-aware, not path-only)
GET /models and /v1/models stay PUBLIC in PR1 (Q3: /models flip deferred; no --auth-public-models flag)
/health and /v1/health remain public by default

features.title: Authn/authz middleware chain on existing API keys
features.description: Replace the middleware_validate_api_key lambda/call (server-http.cpp:208-253, used at :305) with a thin middleware_authz call site that delegates to server_auth::authorize_request(method, req.path, Authorization, X-Api-Key). Decisions: 401 unauthenticated, 403 insufficient perms, 400 malformed path, allow classified+authorized. See docs/design/pr1-rbac-core.md sections 7,8,9.

res.status and the JSON body 'code' always agree (both from the same error_type mapping)
no key, Authorization header, or X-Api-Key value is ever logged
existing test_security.py assertions (including GET /models public) keep passing unchanged

features.title: Principal propagation to handlers
features.description: authorize_request builds a full server_auth_principal {authenticated, subject, issuer, roles[], perms, method, expires_at} (replacing PR1's unused single-role field) and stashes it in a thread_local (server-auth.cpp). reset_principal() is the FIRST line of pre_routing_handler (clear-on-ENTRY, PLAN.md 4.2b) so an early-returning skip path (OPTIONS/503/frontend-asset) cannot leak a prior request's principal on a reused worker thread. get/post/del copy current_principal() into a new server_http_req::principal field (in-class default; assigned after aggregate construction). The gcp /predict internal_req (server-http.cpp:795-803) runs on a std::async worker with NO valid thread_local, so it carries the outer req.principal by value copy. authorize_request signature changes to take a server_auth_request DTO (method, raw_path, authorization, x_api_key, peer_addr, x_auth_subject, x_auth_roles). API-key subject = 'apikey:' + sha256_hex(key).substr(0,12), never the raw key. See docs/design/pr2-principal-proxy.md sections 2,3,4.
acceptance_criteria: server_http_req.principal reflects the current request's resolved identity for every route that constructs a server_http_req (get/post/del); API-key requests show method=AUTH_API_KEY and a non-empty subject 'apikey:<12hex>' derived from SHA-256, never the raw key

no stale principal leaks across requests on a reused worker thread: with --threads-http 1, an authenticated (admin) request followed by an ANONYMOUS request to a PROTECTED route (GET /slots) yields subject_hash=anonymous on the /slots audit line and 401 (thread_local cleared on ENTRY, not exit). Public routes are not audited under 3c so the probe uses /slots, not /health

the accessor is principal_at_construction() (1c): valid only synchronously at get/post/del construction; handlers read req.principal only, never the accessor (no lazy read during streaming/on_complete/gcp async)

the gcp /predict internal dispatch (AIP_MODE=PREDICTION) carries the outer request's principal by value copy (async worker has no thread_local); the PR1 S1 is_infer_only guard still rejects non-INFER @requestFormat

authorize_request takes a server_auth_request DTO and preserves every PR1 decision (auth-disabled allow; anonymous->401 on protected/unclassified/unmatched; authenticated-underprivileged->403; malformed path->400)
server_auth_principal carries subject/issuer/roles[]/perms/method/expires_at; expires_at is always 0 in PR2 (OIDC populates it in PR4)
features.reviewer_notes: Verified against design and PR1 preservation: reset_principal() is the true first statement of pre_routing_handler (before CORS/OPTIONS/state/frontend carve-outs, confirmed by reading server-http.cpp:261-298); principal copied by value into server_http_req at all three get/post/del construction sites and into the gcp internal_req (no thread_local read on the async worker); principal_at_construction() contract documented and not read lazily anywhere. Live-tested (no model, router mode): CIDR/audit fail-closed paths, trusted-proxy allow/deny, and stale-principal-safe entry-clear behavior. One cross-cutting defect found in the same diff (see F006 reviewer_notes) was fixed: an invalid-UTF-8 request path with --auth-audit-log enabled crashed the request to HTTP 500 instead of returning the correct authz decision - fixed by reusing safe_json_to_str (replace-on-invalid-UTF-8) and wrapping audit_emit in try/catch so a hostile path can never alter or fail the request (fail-open restored). No design-level problem found; clean to advance to testing.

features.title: Audit log
features.description: Optional JSON-lines stream via --auth-audit-log PATH (env LLAMA_ARG_AUTH_AUDIT_LOG). audit_emit() is called at every authorize_request return site EXCEPT a matched-PERM_PUBLIC allow (3c: /health etc. not audited), writing one line: ts (ISO-8601 UTC), subject_hash (sha256_hex(subject+salt) or 'anonymous'), method, path (normalized; raw on 400), decision (allow/deny), required_perm (perm name or ''), auth_method (none/api_key/trusted_proxy), peer_ip, request_id ('req-'+random_string()). Append mode, no rotation in PR2. Thread-safe via std::mutex; NO per-line flush (3c: rely on ofstream buffering, flush at exit) to avoid a health-poller DoS. Synchronous; write failure drops lines and NEVER fails the request (fail-open). Salt: LLAMA_AUTH_AUDIT_SALT env if set else per-process random_string(); salt never logged. json::dump escapes control chars so a %0A path cannot inject a second line. Unopenable file aborts startup. Opens independently of g_auth_enabled (audit alone does not enable enforcement). MUST NOT log tokens, Authorization/X-Api-Key, raw X-Auth-Subject, prompts, or DNs. See docs/design/pr2-principal-proxy.md sections 5,7.
acceptance_criteria: tests read the audit file AFTER server.stop() (no per-line flush under 3c); every NON-PUBLIC decision emits exactly one JSON line with all nine fields (ts, subject_hash, method, path, decision, required_perm, auth_method, peer_ip, request_id)
both allow and deny are logged: user key -> /slots yields one deny line (required_perm=READ_STATE); admin key -> /slots yields one allow line; a 400 malformed path (//slots) yields a deny line
3c: public routes are NOT audited - a burst of GET /health and GET /v1/health produces zero audit lines
log-injection safety: a path containing %0A (decodes to a literal newline) still produces a SINGLE JSON line (json::dump escapes it); parsing each physical line yields exactly one JSON object
grep of the audit file for a configured API key, its Bearer header value, a raw X-Auth-Subject value, and any request-body substring returns nothing
subject_hash is stable for the same key within one process run and differs from the raw subject; with LLAMA_AUTH_AUDIT_SALT set it is stable across restarts; the salt is never written
path field is the normalized path on non-400 lines; an unopenable --auth-audit-log path aborts startup; --auth-audit-log alone (no key/policy/proxies) still logs and does NOT enable enforcement
features.reviewer_notes: BLOCKER found and fixed directly: audit_emit() called nlohmann json::dump() with the default strict UTF-8 error handler. A request whose percent-decoded path contains invalid UTF-8 bytes (e.g. GET /%C0%80slots, live-tested) threw a json::type_error inside audit_emit; this propagated out of authorize_request (violating its 'never throws' contract) and out of the pre_routing middleware, turning the correct 401/403/200 decision into an HTTP 500 - and the audit line for that request was lost, contradicting the fail-open requirement and the 'audit must never fail the request' hard rule. Fixed by reusing the existing safe_json_to_str() helper (server-common.cpp, dump with error_handler_t::replace) instead of a raw line.dump() call, and wrapping the whole audit_emit body in try/catch so no future field addition can regress this. Re-tested live: the same request now returns 401 and produces one valid JSON audit line with the invalid bytes replaced. Also fixed a lesser defect: in auth-disabled mode, a NORM_UNMATCHED path (outside api_prefix) was audited with an empty path field because normalize_path only writes out_normalized on NORM_OK; now the raw path is used for the audit line in that case (verified live: /outside-prefix now logs path=/outside-prefix, not empty). Everything else verified clean: request-id/ts/decision/required_perm/auth_method/peer_ip fields exact per design; PERM_PUBLIC matched-allow not audited while non-public health-adjacent unmatched paths still audited per design's 'still audit' rule in auth-disabled mode; no raw subject/roles/keys/headers logged (grepped audit output); salt only from env or per-process random, never logged; unopenable audit path aborts startup (live-tested); no per-line flush, mutex-guarded append confirmed in source.
features.done_summary: PR2 verified: build clean; full auth regression 81/81 (path 31, authz 1, security 30, trusted-proxy 13, audit 6). Rebase tripwire, /0+malformed-CIDR startup abort, RBAC-via-proxy admin/user differentiation, api-key precedence, audit no-secrets + %0A single-line + invalid-UTF-8 fail-open all green.

features.title: Trusted-proxy mode (variant B)
features.description: --auth-trusted-proxies CIDR[,...] (env LLAMA_ARG_AUTH_TRUSTED_PROXIES), IPv4+IPv6, parsed via inet_pton into {family,net[16],bits}; malformed CIDR aborts startup; a /0 all-peers entry is REJECTED at init (2c). resolve_principal precedence (PR2 subset of mTLS->OIDC->proxy-headers->API-key): if peer_is_trusted(req.remote_addr) AND X-Auth-Subject present, build an AUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY principal with subject=X-Auth-Subject, roles=split_csv(X-Auth-Roles) mapped to perms via the persisted policy role table g_role_perms (unknown roles contribute no perms -> fail-closed 403); else fall through to API-key auth. Q4: p.roles keeps raw client role names for audit only; authorization is ONLY on p.perms, never role names. 4b: init MUST change the PR1 early return to `!has_api_keys && !has_trusted_proxies` so trusted-proxy-only mode still builds g_role_perms and sets g_auth_enabled true. peer_is_trusted returns false when no CIDR is configured or the peer is unix/empty/hostname; handles IPv4-mapped ::ffff: peers; 127.0.0.1 and ::1 are distinct families. INVARIANT (Q2): req.remote_addr is the genuine TCP peer only because llama-server never calls httplib set_trusted_proxies - guarded by a required pytest rebase tripwire. HARD RULE: X-Auth-Subject/X-Auth-Roles/X-Forwarded-Client-Cert are ALWAYS stripped in get_headers() (case-insensitive) so handlers/MCP never see them, trusted or not; the middleware is the only reader and gates on peer. Setting --auth-trusted-proxies ENABLES enforcement (Q5). X-Forwarded-Client-Cert is stripped only (consumed in PR3). See docs/design/pr2-principal-proxy.md sections 6,8.
acceptance_criteria: identity headers from a NON-listed peer are ignored and stripped: with --auth-trusted-proxies 10.0.0.0/8, a loopback request carrying X-Auth-Subject/X-Auth-Roles:admin gets no admin access (falls back to API-key auth; POST /slots -> 401/403) and audit auth_method is not trusted_proxy

identity headers from a LISTED peer produce an authenticated principal with mapped roles: with --auth-trusted-proxies 127.0.0.0/8, a loopback request with X-Auth-Subject:ops, X-Auth-Roles:admin can POST /slots/0 (ADMIN_STATE) with no API key; audit shows auth_method=trusted_proxy

REBASE TRIPWIRE (Q2, REQUIRED - do not mark done without it): with --auth-trusted-proxies set to a DIFFERENT host's IP, a request from the non-listed test client sending X-Forwarded-For:<that IP> + X-Auth-Roles:admin still gets 401/403 on POST /slots/0 and audit auth_method is not trusted_proxy (catches a future rebase that lets httplib rewrite remote_addr from X-Forwarded-For)

4b: trusted-proxy-only mode (no --api-key, no --auth-policy-file, only --auth-trusted-proxies 127.0.0.0/8) enforces deny-by-default and maps X-Auth-Roles:admin to the compiled-in admin perm set (g_role_perms populated, g_auth_enabled true)
X-Auth-Roles listing only an unknown role -> authenticated but 403 on a protected route (perms=0); authorization is on perms, never role names
with NO --auth-trusted-proxies configured, identity headers are always ignored/stripped (loopback client with X-Auth-Roles:admin still 401/403 on /slots)
IPv6: ::1/128 trusts an IPv6 loopback peer; a v4-mapped ::ffff:127.0.0.1 peer matches a 127.0.0.0/8 v4 CIDR; a malformed CIDR AND an all-peers /0 (0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0) both abort startup (2c)
X-Auth-Subject/X-Auth-Roles/X-Forwarded-Client-Cert never reach a handler or the MCP proxy header map; trusted-proxy mode is unusable over a unix-socket listener (peer has no IP)
features.reviewer_notes: No implementation defects found in the F007-specific code (init's 4b fix, CIDR parse incl. /0 rejection and stoi-exception handling, peer_is_trusted, v4-mapped stripping, resolve_principal precedence and unknown-role fail-closed perms=0, get_headers case-insensitive strip of X-Auth-Subject/X-Auth-Roles/X-Forwarded-Client-Cert). Live-verified: malformed CIDR and 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 abort startup; trusted-proxy-only mode (no keys/policy) enforces deny-by-default (anonymous GET /slots -> 401) and maps X-Auth-Roles:admin via the compiled-in role table (reached the handler, i.e. authorized) while an unknown-role-only header set gets 403; identity headers from a non-listed peer (127.0.0.0/8 configured, 10.0.0.0/8 required) are ignored, falling back to anonymous/401. req.remote_addr invariant (Q2) confirmed by grep: server-http.cpp/server.cpp never call httplib set_trusted_proxies; the required pytest rebase-tripwire test itself is test-planner/test-runner scope, not yet executed - flagging so it is not skipped when tests are written. Depends on F005's principal plumbing and F006's audit fix, both verified above; no separate F007 defect.

features.title: mTLS TLS-context: SSLServer client-CA construction + SSL_CTX hardening + build gating
features.description: New file pair server-mtls.{h,cpp}. server_mtls::configure(params, out) builds and validates a server_mtls_config {enabled, require_cert, client_ca_file, client_ca_dir, verify_depth, min_tls_version} from the F008a flags: off->disabled (CA files ignored with a warning); optional->enabled,require_cert=false; required->enabled,require_cert=true; optional/required require a CA file or dir else fail; unknown --mtls-required or --tls-min-version, or negative verify-depth, fail (fail closed, never throws). configure ALWAYS populates cfg.min_tls_version even when mode==off (S2). server_mtls::harden_context(void* ctx, cfg) applies to ANY SSL server (mTLS or plain): casts tls_context() (NOT ssl_context() - see design discrepancy table) to SSL_CTX* under CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT, ALWAYS sets SSL_CTX_set_min_proto_version, and ONLY when cfg.enabled sets SSL_CTX_set_verify_depth plus (optional mode) re-sets SSL_VERIFY_PEER WITHOUT SSL_VERIFY_FAIL_IF_NO_PEER_CERT; returns false without OpenSSL (fail closed). server-http.cpp:108-127 SSL construction is extended: build cfg via configure (return false on failure); when mtls enabled use the 4-arg SSLServer(cert,key,ca_file,ca_dir) (httplib sets SSL_VERIFY_PEER|FAIL_IF_NO_PEER_CERT) else the 2-arg plain SSLServer, check srv->is_valid(), then call harden_context via static_cast<httplib::SSLServer*>(srv.get())->tls_context() on BOTH SSL paths (S2: so --tls-min-version applies to plain HTTPS, which httplib otherwise hardcodes to TLS1.2 at httplib.cpp:13298); mtls enabled without server cert/key => refuse start; no-SSL build with any mtls/ssl flag => refuse start. server-mtls.h stays OpenSSL-free (void* handles); OpenSSL include is inside CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT in the .cpp only. Add server-mtls.cpp/.h to CMakeLists llama-server-impl. See docs/design/pr3-mtls.md section 3, 11.
acceptance_criteria: required mode: a client presenting no cert is rejected at the TLS handshake (transport error), not with an HTTP status

features.title: mTLS client-certificate identity extraction into the auth DTO
features.description: server_mtls::extract_identity(const void* ssl_session, mtls_identity& out) extracts SAN URI (first) then SAN DNS (first), never CN, from the already-chain-verified peer cert. Uses the vendored httplib backend-agnostic abstraction httplib::tls::get_peer_cert_from_session(req.ssl) -> PeerCert::sans() (SanType::URI/DNS), gated on CPPHTTPLIB_SSL_ENABLED (design discrepancy: Request.ssl is tls::const_session_t/const void*, NOT SSL*; there is no manual GENERAL_NAMES walk). C1: SAN order is cert-author-controlled, so extract counts each selected type and, if MORE THAN ONE URI (or DNS) SAN is present, leaves that identity field EMPTY (ambiguous -> fail-closed -> perms=0 -> 403); exactly-one -> that value. mtls_identity {present, san_uri, san_dns} carries NO cn/DN field (PII). Returns false (out.present=false) when there is no TLS session or no peer cert (optional mode). Add three fields to server_auth_request (mtls_present, mtls_san_uri, mtls_san_dns) with defaults so existing DTO construction compiles. In server-http.cpp middleware_authz (215-235), after the existing DTO assignments and inside #ifdef CPPHTTPLIB_SSL_ENABLED, call extract_identity(req.ssl, id) and copy id.* into ar.mtls_*. No cert parsing in server-http.cpp. See docs/design/pr3-mtls.md section 4.
acceptance_criteria: a request with a valid client cert populates ar.mtls_present=true and ar.mtls_san_uri (and ar.mtls_san_dns when a DNS SAN is present); CN is never read

C1: a cert carrying two or more URI SANs (or two or more DNS SANs) leaves that identity field EMPTY (present=true but san_uri/san_dns empty) so the identity is treated as ambiguous and denied downstream, not resolved to the first SAN
a request with no TLS session or no peer cert (optional mode, no cert) leaves ar.mtls_present=false and the SAN fields empty
mtls_identity carries no CN/DN field; extraction reads only SANs from the verified cert and does not re-verify the chain
server-auth.h server_auth_request gains mtls_present/mtls_san_uri/mtls_san_dns with in-class defaults so existing construction still compiles
the only server-http.cpp change is the extract_identity call site inside #ifdef CPPHTTPLIB_SSL_ENABLED; no X.509 parsing lives in server-http.cpp
features.reviewer_notes: TWO real defects found and fixed directly (not the coder's stated reasons, which were incorrect diagnoses of a genuine compile/logic bug): (1) the coder bypassed server_mtls::extract_identity entirely and re-implemented SAN extraction plus the C1 ambiguous-SAN counting inline in server-http.cpp's middleware_authz using req.peer_cert(), leaving extract_identity dead code, and did so with NO #ifdef guard at all around the httplib::tls types/req.peer_cert() call - this would fail to compile on a no-SSL build (confirmed: a from-scratch cmake -DLLAMA_OPENSSL=OFF build of the original code would not compile server-http.cpp). (2) investigating why the coder felt forced to bypass extract_identity, found the ACTUAL root cause: server-mtls.cpp guarded its `#include "vendor/cpp-httplib/httplib.h"` on `#ifdef CPPHTTPLIB_SSL_ENABLED`, but that macro is defined *inside* httplib.h itself (derived from CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT/MBEDTLS/WOLFSSL) - it is never defined before this guard runs, so the include (and therefore extract_identity's entire CPPHTTPLIB_SSL_ENABLED-gated body) was permanently compiled out on every build, making extract_identity silently and permanently return present=false regardless of build configuration. Live-confirmed with debug tracing on a full OpenSSL build before the fix: extract_ret=0 on every request despite a valid, verified client cert being presented (curl handshake showed Certificate/CertVerify/Finished exchanged). OIDC hardening pass (S-1/S-2/C-1/C-2/C-4) applied directly in server-oidc.cpp after challenger cleared the design/implementation boundary with NO blocker (35/35 test_oidc.py + 138 passed/1 xfailed full regression at the time of that review). Four non-blocking findings fixed: (S-1) expiry-triggered JWKS refresh had no backoff against a down IdP - every validate() past TTL expiry re-entered refresh_jwks() (a blocking 5s HTTPS GET under g_jwks_mtx) on every request; fixed by anchoring jwks_cache.last_refresh on the ATTEMPT (not just success, matching the design doc's own field comment) and gating the expiry-refresh branch in jwks_get_key on a new g_jwks_refresh_min_interval (default 30s, test-overridable via LLAMA_OIDC_JWKS_REFRESH_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS), fail-static preserved between attempts. (S-2) the 1 MiB JWKS/discovery body cap was checked AFTER the whole body was buffered in https_get - fixed by calling httplib's own cli.set_payload_max_length(1 MiB) before the GET, which aborts the read mid-stream once the cap is exceeded (verified via httplib.cpp: send_() returns res=nullptr on abort, so the existing !res check already treats it as a fetch failure); applies to every https_get call site (discovery + jwks fetch + refetch) since they share the one helper. (C-1) Cache-Control max-age was applied verbatim with no ceiling (a compromised IdP could pin keys for ~31 years via max-age=999999999); fixed by clamping in get_cache_ttl to a new g_jwks_ttl_ceiling (default 86400s/24h, test-overridable via LLAMA_OIDC_JWKS_TTL_CEILING_SECONDS), applied to both the response max-age and the fallback TTL. (C-2) discovery did not verify the discovery doc's 'issuer' field matched --oidc-issuer (OIDC Discovery mandates this); fixed by failing init closed on a missing/mismatched issuer field, checked before jwks_uri is ever used. (C-4, trivial) looks_like_jwt tightened to reject '=' anywhere (real unpadded JWT segments never contain it), now [A-Za-z0-9_-] only. Added 4 new regression tests to test_oidc.py, reusing the existing mock-IdP fixture: test_s1_expiry_refresh_bounded_hits_against_down_idp (burst of 6 requests past TTL expiry against a down IdP yields at most 1 outbound JWKS hit, fail-static preserved throughout), test_s2_oversized_jwks_response_fails_closed_at_boot (2 MiB JWKS body over the 1 MiB cap -> mandatory initial fetch fails -> server refuses to start, fail-closed), test_c1_max_age_ceiling_clamps_runaway_cache_control (max-age=999999999 clamped to a 1s test ceiling; the unknown-kid refresh path is deliberately 'burned' on a throwaway kid first so it cannot confound the result - the rotated kid2 becoming reachable is attributable only to the TTL-expiry path, proving the clamp actually shortened the TTL), test_c2_discovery_issuer_mismatch_fails_startup (discovery doc issuer != --oidc-issuer -> server refuses to start). features.description: Implement server_oidc::init config resolution and the JWKS cache in server-oidc.cpp, all under #ifdef CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT (no-OpenSSL: init returns false when configured). init: no-op+true when not configured; parse oidc_algs into a set (only RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512 allowed; none or HS* -> fail; empty -> default RS256,ES256); parse oidc_audience via the split helper (>=1 required, else fail); clamp oidc_clock_skew to [0,300] (>300 -> fail); resolve g_jwks_url: --oidc-jwks-url wins, else DISCOVERY GET {issuer trimmed of trailing '/'}/.well-known/openid-configuration and read jwks_uri (required string; malformed/failed discovery -> fail); the JWKS and discovery URLs MUST be https (http -> fail, stricter than common_http_client); then a MANDATORY initial JWKS fetch (fail -> return false; PLAN 4.2c). features.title: OIDC JWT verification core (alg whitelist, signature, iss/aud/exp/nbf/iat, typ)
features.description: Implement server_oidc::validate in a fixed, testable order under #ifdef CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT (else return ok=false). Split of responsibility: OUR code enforces shape, the alg whitelist + none/HS* rejection, kid resolution, aud containment, and optional typ; jwt-cpp enforces signature, iss (with_issuer), and exp/nbf/iat with leeway. Order: (1) looks_like_jwt shape check; (2) jwt::decode<traits> (any throw -> deny); (3) read header alg+kid (missing alg or kid -> deny); (4) ALG WHITELIST: reject 'none', reject any 'HS*' (a JWKS public key must never be used as an HMAC secret - algorithm confusion), and require alg in g_oidc_algs; (5) jwks_get_key(kid) (rate-limited refresh on miss, from F009b) -> deny on unknown kid; (6) build a jwt::verify<traits> that allow_algorithm ONLY the single asymmetric verifier for the header alg using the public key from the JWK (NEVER an HMAC verifier), .leeway(g_oidc_clock_skew), and .with_issuer(g_oidc_issuer) when non-empty; verifier.verify(decoded) (throws -> deny); (7) AUDIENCE containment (OURS): the token aud (string or array) must contain >=1 configured audience, else deny; (8) optional typ: when g_oidc_require_at_jwt_typ (set via server_oidc::set_require_typ, called by server-auth), require header typ=='at+jwt'; (9) fill subject(sub; missing->deny), issuer(verified g_oidc_issuer), expires_at(exp as unix seconds; missing exp->deny), claims_json(jwt-cpp get_payload()). Use jwt-cpp helpers to turn a JWK into the asymmetric key; do NOT build an EVP_PKEY by hand; a JWK jwt-cpp cannot turn into a key is treated as unknown-kid (fail closed). error strings are short and NEVER contain the token. Add set_require_typ(bool) to the interface. See docs/design/pr4-oidc.md sections 4.3, 4.4.
features.reviewer_notes: No defects specific to validate() itself; it matches the design's fixed order exactly (shape -> decode -> alg+kid extraction -> alg whitelist reject none/HS* before key lookup -> jwks_get_key -> pinned 6-way switch -> verifier.verify -> aud containment -> optional typ -> fill sub/iss/exp/claims_json), all inside one try/catch that maps any jwt-cpp throw to ok=false/error='verify failed' (no fail-open path: every early return sets v.error and returns v with ok still false). S2 pinned-verifier confirmed by reading: the switch on `alg` is exhaustive over exactly RS256/384/512/ES256/384/512, each branch constructs exactly one jwt::algorithm::rsXXX{pem,...}/esXXX{pem,...}, there is no default/fallthrough that could reach a generic or HMAC verifier, and the alg whitelist (step 4, reject none/HS*, require membership in g_oidc_algs) runs strictly BEFORE jwks_get_key and the switch - so an HS256 token can never reach key lookup, let alone have the RSA PEM handed to an HMAC verifier. jwk_to_pem (F009b, shared code) correctly rejects kty=='oct' outright (returns nullopt, never even attempts a key build) and RSA/EC-vs-wrong-alg-family mismatches fail at PEM/verifier construction time inside the outer try/catch (caught, denied) - confirmed this is genuine fail-closed behavior, not merely 'probably throws'. features.title: OIDC roles-claim mapping, policy oidc parse, resolve_principal branch, init enforcement-flip
features.description: Wire OIDC into the auth decision in server-auth.{h,cpp}. Add AUTH_OIDC to server_auth_method (after AUTH_MTLS, stable values) and AUTH_OIDC->'oidc' to auth_method_to_string (server-auth.cpp:383). Add file-scope state g_oidc_enabled, g_oidc_roles_claim (default 'realm_access.roles'), g_oidc_role_map (claim-role -> perms), g_oidc_require_typ. Parse an optional policy oidc object in init AFTER g_role_perms is persisted (next to the mtls parse ~server-auth.cpp:711): roles_claim (string, default), role_map (EXACT match only, no wildcards; each value must be an existing role else fail), require_at_jwt_typ (bool default false). init enforcement flip (S1 pattern, parallel to mTLS): has_oidc=server_oidc::configured(params) near line 540; extend the auth-disabled early return at 657 with '&& !has_oidc'; OR has_oidc into g_auth_enabled at 669; after the oidc policy parse call server_oidc::set_require_typ(g_oidc_require_typ) and if(has_oidc) { if(!server_oidc::init(params)) return false; g_oidc_enabled=true; }; add the LAST-check S1 guard 'if (has_oidc && !g_auth_enabled) { SRV_ERR; return false; }' next to the mtls guard at 857. extract_oidc_roles(claims_json, path): json::parse in try (parse error->{}), dot-split path walking objects, terminal array->string elements or single string->{that}, else {} (fail closed). resolve_principal (server-auth.cpp:933): insert the OIDC branch AFTER trusted-proxy (~978) and BEFORE API-key (~980) - new precedence mTLS -> trusted-proxy -> OIDC -> API-key -> anonymous: if g_oidc_enabled, strip 'Bearer ' from req.authorization (OIDC reads Authorization only, not X-Api-Key); if non-empty AND looks_like_jwt -> server_oidc::validate; on ok build AUTH_OIDC principal (authenticated, issuer=v.issuer, subject=v.subject, expires_at=v.expires_at, roles=extract_oidc_roles, perms=OR of g_oidc_role_map for known roles, unknown->nothing); on JWT-shaped-but-invalid return anonymous (401) with NO api-key fallback (OQ3); if not JWT-shaped fall through to API-key. features.done_summary: OIDC hardening pass (S-1/S-2/C-1/C-2/C-4) applied directly in server-oidc.cpp after challenger cleared the design/implementation boundary with NO blocker (35/35 test_oidc.py + 138 passed/1 xfailed full regression at the time of that review). Four non-blocking findings fixed: (S-1) expiry-triggered JWKS refresh had no backoff against a down IdP - every validate() past TTL expiry re-entered refresh_jwks() (a blocking 5s HTTPS GET under g_jwks_mtx) on every request; fixed by anchoring jwks_cache.last_refresh on the ATTEMPT (not just success, matching the design doc's own field comment) and gating the expiry-refresh branch in jwks_get_key on a new g_jwks_refresh_min_interval (default 30s, test-overridable via LLAMA_OIDC_JWKS_REFRESH_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS), fail-static preserved between attempts. (S-2) the 1 MiB JWKS/discovery body cap was checked AFTER the whole body was buffered in https_get - fixed by calling httplib's own cli.set_payload_max_length(1 MiB) before the GET, which aborts the read mid-stream once the cap is exceeded (verified via httplib.cpp: send_() returns res=nullptr on abort, so the existing !res check already treats it as a fetch failure); applies to every https_get call site (discovery + jwks fetch + refetch) since they share the one helper. (C-1) Cache-Control max-age was applied verbatim with no ceiling (a compromised IdP could pin keys for ~31 years via max-age=999999999); fixed by clamping in get_cache_ttl to a new g_jwks_ttl_ceiling (default 86400s/24h, test-overridable via LLAMA_OIDC_JWKS_TTL_CEILING_SECONDS), applied to both the response max-age and the fallback TTL. (C-2) discovery did not verify the discovery doc's 'issuer' field matched --oidc-issuer (OIDC Discovery mandates this); fixed by failing init closed on a missing/mismatched issuer field, checked before jwks_uri is ever used. (C-4, trivial) looks_like_jwt tightened to reject '=' anywhere (real unpadded JWT segments never contain it), now [A-Za-z0-9_-] only. Added 4 new regression tests to test_oidc.py, reusing the existing mock-IdP fixture: test_s1_expiry_refresh_bounded_hits_against_down_idp (burst of 6 requests past TTL expiry against a down IdP yields at most 1 outbound JWKS hit, fail-static preserved throughout), test_s2_oversized_jwks_response_fails_closed_at_boot (2 MiB JWKS body over the 1 MiB cap -> mandatory initial fetch fails -> server refuses to start, fail-closed), test_c1_max_age_ceiling_clamps_runaway_cache_control (max-age=999999999 clamped to a 1s test ceiling; the unknown-kid refresh path is deliberately 'burned' on a throwaway kid first so it cannot confound the result - the rotated kid2 becoming reachable is attributable only to the TTL-expiry path, proving the clamp actually shortened the TTL), test_c2_discovery_issuer_mismatch_fails_startup (discovery doc issuer != --oidc-issuer -> server refuses to start). Rebuilt both LLAMA_OPENSSL=ON and LLAMA_OPENSSL=OFF: both exit 0, zero new warnings (only the twelve pre-existing vendored jwt-cpp header warnings remain, same as before this pass, not introduced here). Full unit/test_oidc.py run: 39/39 passed (35 pre-existing + 4 new) in a clean 41.94s run; one earlier full-suite run under heavy machine load produced 2 transient timeouts (including test_unknown_kid_rejected, a pre-existing test untouched by this change) that did not reproduce on rerun and passed individually in isolation - confirmed as environmental flakiness, not a defect introduced by this hardening pass.

features.title: mTLS CRL (certificate revocation)
features.description: --mtls-crl-file flag + server_mtls_config.crl_file. CRL must be added to the SAME SSL_CTX default store httplib populates via SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations (obtained via SSL_CTX_get_cert_store), NOT a separate X509_STORE_load_locations call (that cannot prove a CRL was actually loaded - fail-open risk). Parse the CRL PEM explicitly and X509_STORE_add_crl each entry; require >=1 loaded CRL or fail closed at startup. Then set X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK | X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK_ALL on the store. Extends server-mtls.cpp harden_context (reached via static_cast<httplib::SSLServer*>(srv.get())->tls_context(), the existing PR3 path - no new server-http.cpp code). No runtime CRL reload (restart to rotate; short-lived certs recommended instead - OQ-A2). See docs/design/pr5-optional.md sections 0, 2.
features.done_summary: PR5 F010a verified: build clean (LLAMA_OPENSSL on/off); full auth regression 206/206 passed + 1 xfailed incl. test_mtls.py CRL revocation, expiry, multiple-CRL, and flag validation tests. All 9 acceptance criteria green.
acceptance_criteria: a client cert revoked by the configured CRL fails the TLS handshake in both optional and required mTLS mode (assert only that the connection PRESENTING the revoked cert fails; in optional mode the client may still reconnect with no cert as anonymous - challenger R4)
an unrevoked cert from the same issuer still succeeds and the PR3 SAN->role authz is unchanged
--mtls-crl-file pointing at a missing/unparseable file, or a file that parses but contains zero CRLs, aborts startup (fail closed)
--mtls-crl-file set while --mtls-required is off aborts startup
a CRL with NO nextUpdate field aborts startup (challenger R1: no runtime reload means a never-expiring CRL is a silent revocation freeze = fail-open)
a CRL whose nextUpdate is already in the past aborts startup with a clear message (rather than booting and rejecting every mTLS client)

both X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK and X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK_ALL are set (OQ-A1 RESOLVED: keep both; OpenSSL skips a self-signed root in check_revocation, so at the default --mtls-verify-depth 1 exactly ONE CRL from the client CA is required and CRL_CHECK_ALL costs nothing, while at depth>1 it catches a revoked intermediate). Flag help must NOT claim a self-signed root needs its own CRL (challenger R2)
no --mtls-crl-file set: behavior identical to pre-F010a (no regression to existing mtls tests)

Store choice confirmed correct per R5: SSL_CTX_get_cert_store(c) on the same ctx httplib already populated via SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations, not a separate X509_STORE_load_locations call. Both X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK and X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK_ALL are set only after count>=1 confirmed CRLs loaded (count==0 -> fail closed, matches acceptance criterion). configure() rejects --mtls-crl-file with --mtls-required off before any TLS work, matching the fail-closed table in section 2.4. features.title: OIDC RFC-7662 opaque-token introspection
features.description: Three new flags: --oidc-introspection-url, --oidc-client-id, --oidc-client-secret-file (secret from FILE only, never argv/env value, never logged). New introspection-only config path (works WITHOUT a JWKS/issuer). New hardened POST+basic-auth helper (introspect_post) separate from the existing GET-only https_get; reuses the same TLS hardening (https-only, no redirects, timeouts, body-size cap) established for JWKS in F009b. Token-hash cache: positive results cached with TTL <= min(exp, 60s); negative results cached g_introspect_neg_ttl (~5s); network/parse errors NOT cached (retried next request - OQ-B3, confirm). Reuses AUTH_OIDC enum (no new enum value - OQ-B4, confirm) with issuer set from the token's iss or the introspection URL; resolve_principal gets a new opaque-bearer branch. has_oidc in server-auth.cpp:546 widens to include introspection-configured. Roles extracted via the existing g_oidc_roles_claim/extract_oidc_roles machinery (does NOT split an RFC7662 scope string by default - OQ-B2, confirm or extend). See docs/design/pr5-optional.md sections 0, 3.
features.done_summary: PR5 F010b verified: build clean (LLAMA_OPENSSL on/off); full auth regression 206/206 passed + 1 xfailed incl. test_oidc.py introspection, rate-limiting, cache TTL, aud/iss/exp/nbf validation, and cross-service token-replay blocker tests. All 12 acceptance criteria green.
acceptance_criteria: BLOCKER B1 (challenger, binding): --oidc-audience is REQUIRED when introspection is configured, and the introspection response's aud (string or array) must intersect the configured audiences; absent/mistyped/non-intersecting aud -> 401. Without this, any active token from the same IdP realm issued to a DIFFERENT client is accepted here (cross-service token replay -> privilege escalation)

BLOCKER B1 (cont.): when --oidc-issuer is also set, the response iss must equal it (absent or mismatched -> 401); a response with exp already past (exp + clock_skew <= now) or nbf in the future -> 401

BLOCKER B2 (challenger, binding): introspection POSTs are globally rate-limited (fixed window, default 20/s, env-overridable) and the token-hash cache has a hard size cap (4096) with expired-entry sweeping; the outbound POST is issued WITHOUT holding the cache mutex. resolve_principal runs before route classification, so an unauthenticated request to a PUBLIC route carrying any Bearer header would otherwise be an IdP amplification and unbounded-memory vector

OQ-B1 RESOLVED (binding): the introspection branch sits AFTER the API-key branch (precedence mTLS -> trusted-proxy -> OIDC JWT -> API key -> introspection -> anonymous), triggers only on an Authorization value starting with 'Bearer ', and on failure falls through only to anonymous/401. Test: with both --api-key and introspection configured, 'Authorization: Bearer <valid-api-key>' authenticates as api_key with ZERO hits on the mock introspection endpoint

a policy default_role combined with --oidc-introspection-url aborts startup (otherwise the api-key branch authorizes every unknown bearer with the default role and introspection is never reached - total bypass; challenger R12 item 6)
a valid opaque bearer token (active:true, matching aud, mapped role) is authorized per its mapped permissions; unmapped/absent roles -> authenticated with perms=0 -> 403 (never a default role)
introspection returning active:false, active:true without sub, a network/HTTP error, a redirect, or a non-200 yields 401

the client secret is read from --oidc-client-secret-file (binary read, ALL trailing CR/LF stripped, interior newline = fail closed) and never appears in argv, env dump, error strings, or logs; a URL containing userinfo (@ in the authority) aborts startup; client_id containing ':' or non-printable bytes aborts startup; introspect_post never logs the URL

the token value is percent-encoded into the form body by a local RFC 3986 encoder (NOT httplib::detail::encode_query_param, which is not declared in the vendored header and is an internal API); tokens >4096 bytes or outside the RFC 6750 b64token charset are denied with no network call
introspection requests are POST over HTTPS only, with the same no-redirect/timeout/1MiB-body-cap hardening as JWKS fetches; the cache key is the token SHA-256, never the raw token

positive cache entries expire at min(exp - now, 60s), negatives (including B1-check denials) at ~5s, transient errors and rate-limit rejections are NOT cached; repeated identical requests within the positive window do not re-hit the endpoint (verified via the mock's request count, with LLAMA_OIDC_INTROSPECT_*_TTL_SECONDS env overrides making it deterministic - challenger R8)

S1 enforcement flip is complete and asserted: has_introspect widens the auth-disabled early return AND is OR'd into g_auth_enabled AND 'has_introspect && !g_auth_enabled' aborts startup; g_oidc_enabled stays gated on has_oidc ALONE and g_introspect_enabled on has_introspect ALONE (conflating them silently locks out JWT-shaped bearers in introspection-only mode)

introspection-only mode (no --oidc-issuer, no --oidc-jwks-url) enforces auth, introspects ANY Bearer including a JWT-shaped one, and on a build without OpenSSL aborts startup (the server-oidc.cpp #else stub must not early-return true - challenger R6)

OQ-B2 RESOLVED: extract_oidc_roles splits a terminal STRING claim on whitespace when the last segment of the claim path is exactly 'scope' or 'scp'; every other string claim stays a single role (no regression to existing realm_access.roles tests)
OIDC configured for JWKS-only (no introspection flags) behaves identically to pre-F010b (no regression to test_oidc.py)

features.reviewer_notes: F010b's status was left at 'todo' by the coder despite the code being fully written; corrected to 'testing' after verification below (features.json status transitions must come from reviewer/test-runner, and this is that transition). B1 verified live in code, not just claimed: server_oidc::init moves the audience parse (server-oidc.cpp) OUT of the JWKS-only branch so it runs whenever jwks_cfg || intro_cfg, empty audience aborts startup on either path. introspect() checks aud (string or array, intersect g_oidc_audiences; absent/wrong-typed/non-intersecting -> deny+negative-cache), iss (only when g_oidc_issuer is non-empty; mismatch -> deny), and exp/nbf clock checks (exp+skew<=now or nbf>now+skew -> deny) on the ACTUAL introspection HTTP response body, all before v.ok is ever set true - confirmed by reading the parse block end to end, not trusting a comment. B2 verified: fixed-window rate limiter (g_introspect_window_start/count, default 20/s, env-overridable via LLAMA_OIDC_INTROSPECT_MAX_PER_SECOND) and the 4096 hard cache cap with expired-entry sweep run under g_introspect_mtx; the outbound cli.Post() call in introspect_post is issued strictly outside the lock scope (lock is released at the closing brace before 'B2: POST issued WITHOUT holding mutex', matching the required lock->lookup->unlock->POST->lock->insert->unlock shape) - confirmed by reading the mutex scope, not the comment. Pre-flight token length (4096) and RFC 6750 b64token charset checks run before any cache/network touch. OQ-B1 verified: introspection branch (server-auth.cpp resolve_principal) sits textually and logically after the API-key branch and before the final anonymous return; only Authorization values, only when non-empty, are considered. R12 item 6 (default_role + introspection abort) present at server-auth.cpp. S1 pattern fully wired: has_introspect widens the auth-disabled early return, is OR'd into g_auth_enabled, g_oidc_enabled/g_introspect_enabled are set independently (not conflated) after server_oidc::init succeeds, and the defensive 'has_introspect && !g_auth_enabled -> abort' check is present alongside the mTLS/OIDC ones. REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (functional, would have failed acceptance criterion 'introspection-only mode ... introspects ANY Bearer including a JWT-shaped one'): the resolve_principal introspection branch guarded on '!server_oidc::looks_like_jwt(token)', which is the section-3.4 condition the design's own section 8.5 (ANSWER OQ-B1) explicitly states is WRONG and superseded - in introspection-only mode (g_oidc_enabled==false) a JWT-shaped opaque token would fall through the JWT block (which never runs) and then be skipped by this stale condition, landing on anonymous/401 instead of being introspected. Removed the looks_like_jwt guard so any non-empty Bearer value reaches introspection when g_introspect_enabled, per the binding precedence in 8.5. SECOND DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (code quality, not security): server_oidc::init had a literal duplicated clock-skew-validation block (two copies of the same range check, one mis-indented at the wrong nesting level from an apparent merge artifact between the two coders' JWKS/introspection edits) plus stale 'Step 5'/'Step 6' labels reused twice; removed the duplicate, fixed indentation and step numbering. THIRD: removed a dead 'if (!defined(CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT))' check inside a function that is itself only compiled under CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT (always false, confusing). FOURTH: added a missing explicit '#include <fstream>' for the std::ifstream secret-file read (previously relying on a transitive include). FIFTH (quality): the six introspect() cache-insert call sites duplicated the same lock+sweep+cap+insert block; two of the six negative-cache sites were missing the sweep-before-cap-check step (aud-mismatch/iss-mismatch/exp/nbf/no-sub paths never triggered a sweep, only the active:false and success paths did), meaning once the cache filled with those specific denial types it could stay full and refuse new inserts indefinitely without ever reclaiming expired slots. Extracted a single introspect_cache_insert() helper used by all six sites so every insert now sweeps consistently; this also collapses ~90 lines of duplication, improving AGENTS.md DRY/minimal-footprint compliance. R9 secret hygiene verified: binary ifstream read, all trailing CR/LF stripped, interior newline (or CR) after stripping -> fail closed, printable-ASCII-only check on both client_id (also rejects ':') and secret, userinfo ('@' in authority) rejected at init, introspect_post never logs the URL (only a fixed-format status string would be logged, and no such log line exists in the current code - confirmed by grep for SRV_WRN/SRV_ERR near introspect_post, there are none, matching the design's 'never logs the URL' requirement trivially by having no failure log there at all). features.title: Enforce token exp during long SSE streams
features.description: PLAN.md 8.4 / PR4 residual (challenger C4): authorization is evaluated once, in middleware_authz, so an SSE stream can outlive the access token's exp. PR4 populates server_auth_principal.expires_at from the JWT exp (server-auth.cpp:1152) but nothing re-reads it. ANCHOR CORRECTION: PLAN.md and the previous version of this entry pointed at server-context.cpp's generation loop; that is wrong as the sole site, because in router mode the streaming completion is served by server_http_proxy (server-models.cpp:2073) and never enters handle_completions_impl, and there are four other SSE producers. The gate goes at the single HTTP choke point instead: process_handler_response -> chunked_content_provider (server-http.cpp:598/609), as the first statement before response->next(chunk), using request->principal (F005). New logic lives in server-auth.{h,cpp}: stream_deadline(principal) -> expires_at + grace (0 = never), stream_expired(deadline) -> one std::time() read, and sse_expired_chunk_oai()/_anthropic() returning function-local-static SSE error events. grace = clamp(params.oidc_clock_skew, 0, 300), set at the TOP of server_auth::init (before the auth-disabled early return at server-auth.cpp:692), so the cut uses the same leeway that accepted the token. Cadence: checked once per chunk, no throttle (a time() read is ~ns against a ms token decode). Termination: an SSE error event then sink.done() + return false, reusing the existing mid-stream error convention (server-context.cpp:4248-4257) rather than a silent close; silent close is reserved for client disconnect. server-http.h gains one std::string sse_expired_chunk field on server_http_res (empty = OAI dialect); server-context.cpp gains ONE line setting the Anthropic dialect for TASK_RESPONSE_TYPE_ANTHROPIC after line 4246. Auth-method-agnostic by construction: keys off expires_at only, never on p.method, so F010b introspection is covered with no F013 change. See docs/design/pr5-f013-sse-expiry.md.

All 18 acceptance criteria green; no B1/B2/S2/S3 defects on live code audit.

CHALLENGER B1: the deadline is checked TWICE per provider invocation, once before response->next(chunk) and once after next() returns but before sink.write(); next() blocks for an unbounded time (slot queue, proxy pipe read, tool wait, disabled ping), so a single pre-next check would let a post-deadline chunk be written

CHALLENGER B2: the gate is inert unless response->content_type starts with "text/event-stream"; in router mode server_http_proxy sets next() unconditionally (server-models.cpp:2073) so non-streaming application/json responses are also is_stream(), and SSE framing must never be appended to them. Test: router-mode non-streaming POST /v1/embeddings (or chat/completions with stream:false) whose token expires during the child's compute still returns a well-formed JSON body with no 'data:' bytes

expires_at == 0 is NEVER cut: stream_deadline() returns 0 for it and stream_expired(0) is always false, so an API-key / mTLS / trusted-proxy / auth-disabled long streaming completion runs to its normal 'data: [DONE]' termination (regression guard, must be a pytest)

CHALLENGER S2: stream_deadline() saturates instead of overflowing - a principal with expires_at close to INT64_MAX returns INT64_MAX, never a wrapped negative value (signed overflow here is UB and wraps in the fail-open direction). Verified by code inspection plus a unit-style check if one is cheap

auth-method-agnostic: the F013 code path in server-auth.cpp contains no reference to AUTH_OIDC, p.method, or any auth-method name, so an F010b-introspected opaque token that sets expires_at is covered with zero F013 changes

deadline = principal.expires_at + clamp(params.oidc_clock_skew, 0, 300); the grace is assigned in server_auth::init BEFORE the auth-disabled early return (server-auth.cpp:692-695), so it is never skipped

cadence is std::time(nullptr) reads per chunk-provider invocation with no throttle state and no cached time; the guaranteed property is 'no SSE byte is written at or after the deadline'. The CONNECTION may stay open past the deadline for as long as the producer sits in next(); that duration is caller-influenced (sse_ping_interval is a per-request field, -1 disables pings) and is an accepted residual, NOT bounded by 30s as the first design draft claimed

cut behavior with --oidc-clock-skew 0 and a JWT minted with exp = now+4s: a streaming POST /v1/chat/completions with a large n_predict terminates and the received body contains exactly 'data: {"error":{"code":401,"message":"access token expired","type":"authentication_error"}}\n\n' and does NOT contain 'data: [DONE]'
no false positive: the same server with a JWT minted with exp = now+300s streams the identical request to a normal 'data: [DONE]' termination with no error chunk

skew consistency: with --oidc-clock-skew 60 and a token minted with exp = now-5s (comfortably inside the leeway window, NOT at its edge), the stream is not cut on the first provider invocation and delivers at least one real content chunk

CHALLENGER OQ1: /v1/responses (TASK_RESPONSE_TYPE_OAI_RESP) gets the event-dialect chunk via format_oai_resp_sse, not the bare 'data:' OAI form - a data-only frame is SSE event type 'message' and a Responses client drops it, degrading the cut into the silent truncation the design forbids. Test: streaming POST /v1/responses cut by expiry contains 'event: error'

CHALLENGER S3: server-context.cpp contains ZERO references to server_auth:: - the sse_expired_chunk for the Anthropic and Responses dialects is built inline with format_anthropic_sse / format_oai_resp_sse / format_error_response. server-context.cpp is in the server-context static lib, which does not contain server-auth.cpp and is linked standalone by tests/CMakeLists.txt:163 (test-chat). server_auth::sse_expired_chunk_anthropic() is NOT added to the interface

sse_expired_chunk_oai() is a function-local static built once via format_oai_sse/format_error_response, not rebuilt per chunk and not a hardcoded byte literal

CHALLENGER OQ3: on cut, server_http_res::auth_expired is set and server_res_spipe::on_complete() (server-stream.cpp:631) early-returns after g_stream_sessions.evict_and_cancel(conv_id) instead of draining the rest of the generation into the replay ring buffer. Test: a streaming completion with X-Conversation-Id whose token expires mid-stream is cut, and a subsequent GET /v1/stream?conv_id=... returns 404 rather than continuing to deliver post-expiry output; the slot is released (GET /slots or a following request is served promptly)

the log line emitted on cut is SRV_WRN (a security control firing is not informational) and contains no subject, path, token, DN or Authorization value; no audit_emit line is added and F006's nine audit fields are unchanged

non-streaming responses are unaffected in BOTH single-server and router mode: a non-stream completion whose token expires during generation still returns 200 with the full, parseable body (documented scope decision, enforced by the content-type condition in B2)

features.title: /cors-proxy SSRF hardening (target allowlist + pinned-IP connect)
features.description: PLAN.md 8.1 residual, SCOPE CORRECTED by the PR7 design pass. PERM_PROXY (F002/F003, route table at server-auth.cpp:253-257) answers WHO may proxy; nothing answers WHERE. An authorized caller can reach 169.254.169.254, loopback sidecars and RFC1918 hosts, and can inject arbitrary outbound headers via the x-llama-server-proxy-header-* prefix (server-cors-proxy.h:45-58). ANCHOR CORRECTIONS (verified, do not trust the previous text): (1) the outbound code is the header-only helper server-cors-proxy.h:22-75 (proxy_request), NOT server.cpp - server.cpp:330-337 only registers the route; (2) the HTTP client is built in server_http_proxy's ctor (server-models.cpp:2036-2199), which is SHARED with router-mode child forwarding to CHILD_ADDR 127.0.0.1 (server-models.cpp:1192, :1826), so a guard placed there would break router mode - it MUST live in server-cors-proxy.h; (3) /tools is NOT an SSRF vector and is OUT OF SCOPE: its built-in tools are read_file/glob/grep/exec_shell_command/write_file/edit_file/get_datetime (server-tools.cpp:268-1031) and MCP runs over a stdio subprocess (server-mcp.h:94-125), with zero client-controlled outbound HTTP - this contradicts PLAN.md 8.1 and the previous description. DESIGN: new files server-ssrf.{h,cpp} own all logic; new --proxy-allowed-hosts CSV of hostnames and CIDRs; DENY-BY-DEFAULT (empty allowlist = every proxy request 403), with a compiled-in private/loopback/link-local/ULA/multicast/reserved block layered on top of hostname entries. DNS rebinding is closed by resolving with getaddrinfo, requiring EVERY resolved address to pass, then pinning the first via httplib ClientImpl::set_hostname_addr_map (httplib.h:2341, consumed at httplib.cpp:8911-8920 with AI_NUMERICHOST) so no re-resolve happens at connect; redirects are refused because create_redirect_client/setup_redirect_client (httplib.cpp:9630-9710) does NOT copy addr_map_. See docs/design/pr7-additional-hardening.md section 3.

ROUTER MODE UNBROKEN: server-models.cpp:1192 and :1826 (router -> child forwarding to CHILD_ADDR 127.0.0.1) are byte-identical apart from nothing - they pass no opts and get the defaults (pinned_ip empty, follow_location true). test_router.py passes unchanged with no --proxy-allowed-hosts set
/tools is UNCHANGED by this feature (no server-tools.cpp or server-mcp.cpp edit); the scope correction that /tools performs no client-controlled outbound HTTP is documented in the design

DENY BY DEFAULT: with --ui-mcp-proxy on and --proxy-allowed-hosts unset, GET and POST /cors-proxy to ANY target return 403 with body {"error":{"message":"proxy target not allowed","type":"proxy_target_denied"}}; startup logs one SRV_WRN naming --proxy-allowed-hosts but does NOT abort

private-address block: with --proxy-allowed-hosts set to a HOSTNAME entry whose DNS answer is 127.0.0.1 (or 169.254.169.254, 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, ::1, fe80::/10, fc00::/7), the request is denied - a hostname entry can only reach public addresses

PORT-SCOPED ALLOWLIST (challenger B1-a): entry grammar is target[:portspec] where target is an IPv4/IPv6 literal, a CIDR, a bracketed IPv6 (mandatory when a port is present) or a hostname, and portspec is a decimal port or '*'. An entry with NO portspec permits ONLY ports 80 and 443. '--proxy-allowed-hosts 127.0.0.1/32' therefore does NOT reach 127.0.0.1:6379 or 127.0.0.1:8500; '--proxy-allowed-hosts 127.0.0.1/32:9000' reaches only port 9000. Each ':*' entry is accepted but logs one SRV_WRN at startup naming the entry

DNS-REBINDING/TOCTOU: the connection uses the exact IP that was validated. Verified by a test whose target hostname resolves to an allowed IP at check time and whose second resolution would differ (e.g. a stub resolver or /etc/hosts-style fixture), asserting the request still lands on the first IP; and by code inspection that server_http_proxy sets cli->set_hostname_addr_map({{host, pinned_ip}}) rather than passing a rewritten host string (Host header, SNI and certificate verification must still use the original hostname)

REDIRECT SUPPRESSION + LOCATION STRIP (challenger R-A4): /cors-proxy passes follow_location=false AND strip_location=true. A test target returning 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/ causes status 302 to be relayed with the Location header REMOVED, and NO request is made to the redirect target. Rationale: the WebUI fetch() defaults to redirect:follow and resolves a relative Location against llama-server's own origin, so relaying Location lets an allowlisted-but-hostile target steer the operator's authenticated browser into same-origin requests. Router mode is unaffected (strip_location defaults false)
ALL resolved addresses must pass: a hostname resolving to one permitted and one blocked address is denied (not allowed by picking the good one)

the client-visible 403 body and status are IDENTICAL for every denial reason (not in allowlist / blocked range / resolve failure / bad port / bad hostname), so /cors-proxy is not an internal-network scanner or DNS-existence oracle; the specific reason appears only in an SRV_WRN server log line, which contains at most the requested host and port and NEVER a resolved internal IP

--proxy-allowed-hosts parse is fail-closed at startup: an unparseable entry, a /0 prefix (v4 or v6), a prefix wider than the family (/33 v4, /129 v6), or a hostname entry containing a non-ASCII or control byte, '/', '@', '\\', '?', '#', '[' or ']' each abort startup with SRV_ERR

hostname allowlist matching is exact and ASCII-case-insensitive after stripping at most one trailing dot; there is NO wildcard and NO suffix matching (evil-example.com must not match example.com, and sub.example.com must not match example.com)
IPv4-mapped IPv6 resolution results are unwrapped and evaluated against the IPv4 table, so a target resolving to ::ffff:169.254.169.254 is denied by 169.254.0.0/16

port sanity (challenger R-A3): a URL port outside 1..65535 is denied by the guard with the SAME 403 body as every other denial. Because common_http_parse_url does std::stoi (common/http.h:88) and throws std::out_of_range for e.g. ?url=http://h:99999999999/ (which ex_wrapper maps to 500), proxy_request MUST wrap the common_http_parse_url call in try/catch and return the identical 403 - no malformed URL may produce a 500

the guard is a SECOND, independent layer: a caller WITHOUT PERM_PROXY still gets the RBAC 403 before the guard runs, and a caller WITH PERM_PROXY still gets the guard 403 for a disallowed target (both assertions in the same test file)

features.title: Runtime CRL reload (poll-based, last-known-good on failure)
features.description: F010a residual (OQ-A2, accepted at the time): --mtls-crl-file is loaded once in server-mtls.cpp::load_crl_file (:93-149) via harden_context (:153-194, called from server-http.cpp:154), so rotating a CRL requires a restart. CORRECTION to the task framing: SIGHUP does NOT avoid a worker thread - a signal handler may not open a file, allocate, call OpenSSL or take a mutex, so every correct trigger needs a servicing thread. Given the thread is unavoidable, the design picks a periodic re-stat-and-reload POLL behind a new --mtls-crl-reload-interval SECONDS flag (default 0 = disabled, preserving F010a behaviour exactly), because it needs no change to server.cpp's shared signal handler (server.cpp:26-38, 485-490, assigned in two places at :426 and :475), works on Windows, works with an automated CRL cron, and has zero rebase exposure. CORRECTION on OpenSSL: there is NO safe pointer swap. SSL_CTX_set_cert_store frees the old store and writes a raw pointer that an in-flight X509_STORE_CTX holds without a reference (use-after-free), and add-only X509_STORE_add_crl accumulates stale CRLs that OpenSSL's get_crl_sk can prefer over the fresh one (fail-open). The design instead installs X509_STORE_set_lookup_crls ONCE at startup and swaps only our own shared_ptr snapshot under our own mutex; the callback returns a fresh, up-reffed STACK_OF(X509_CRL) that the caller owns, so there is no cross-thread lifetime question. F010a's X509_STORE_add_crl calls are KEPT as a safety net so a wrong assumption degrades to 'reload is a no-op', never to lost revocation. Bad reload = keep the last-known-good CRL and log SRV_ERR (not abort). See docs/design/pr7-additional-hardening.md section 5.
features.done_summary: PR7 F016 verified: build clean on OpenSSL and no-OpenSSL; full auth regression 242/242 passed + 1 xfailed; CRL poll-reload with last-known-good fallback, session-resumption suppression, callback robustness, and flag validation all green.
acceptance_criteria: all reload logic lives in tools/server/server-mtls.cpp; the new flag in common/arg.cpp and its field in common/common.h are the only other existing-file changes. Per challenger R-C3 the server_http_context::stop() call site is DROPPED: after R-C2 crl_reload_stop() only silences log lines during the last second of shutdown of a detached thread nobody waits on, and removing it removes F016's only touch of an upstream-owned source file

NO REGRESSION when reload is off: with --mtls-crl-reload-interval unset or 0, behaviour is identical to F010a - the existing test_mtls.py CRL revocation, expiry, multiple-CRL and flag-validation tests pass unmodified

F010a's validation is written ONCE: load_crl_file is refactored into crl_parse_file (parse + R1 nextUpdate-present and nextUpdate-not-past checks + count>=1) plus a thin add-to-store wrapper, and the reload path calls the SAME crl_parse_file - a reloaded CRL with no nextUpdate, with a past nextUpdate, that is unparseable, or that contains zero CRLs is rejected by identical logic

CALLBACK IS ACTUALLY CONSULTED (the load-bearing test): start with CRL v1 revoking nothing, confirm client cert C connects; overwrite the file with CRL v2 revoking C; after interval + slack, C's TLS HANDSHAKE FAILS. This proves the lookup callback beats the store-resident v1 CRL. An unrevoked cert D from the same CA still succeeds in the same run

BAD RELOAD KEEPS LAST-KNOWN-GOOD: after the step above, overwrite the file with garbage; after interval + slack the server is STILL RUNNING, C is STILL rejected, D still succeeds, and exactly one SRV_ERR was logged naming the failure. The bad file NEVER becomes the active CRL and revocation is never silently disabled

IN-FLIGHT CONNECTIONS SURVIVE: an established mTLS connection (e.g. a long SSE stream) started before a reload is not closed, reset or re-verified by the reload; only handshakes starting after the swap see the new CRL set. Asserted by a test that holds a stream open across a reload

the reload thread NEVER touches an SSL_CTX, X509_STORE or httplib object after startup - it only parses a file and swaps a shared_ptr under a mutex. Verified by code inspection; this is what makes its lifetime independent of the HTTP server's
no CRL is added to or removed from the SSL_CTX store after startup, and SSL_CTX_set_cert_store / SSL_CTX_set1_cert_store are NOT called anywhere (the rejected, unsafe mechanisms - design section 5.3)

NO 'SAFETY NET' CLAIM (challenger B2): installing X509_STORE_set_lookup_crls REPLACES the store's CRL lookup - the add_crl'd CRLs are reachable ONLY through the default lookup_crls (X509_STORE_CTX_get1_crls), which the custom callback overwrites, so after F016 they are inert. The degenerate failure mode of a broken callback is X509_V_ERR_UNABLE_TO_GET_CRL on every handshake, i.e. FAIL-CLOSED, not 'reload is a no-op'. Instead of a net, bind a real assertion: immediately after X509_STORE_set_lookup_crls, verify X509_STORE_get_lookup_crls(store) == crl_lookup_cb and SRV_ERR + return false if not. The design text and this criterion's previous wording were both wrong and must not be reintroduced

the callback returns an EMPTY STACK_OF(X509_CRL) (never nullptr) when the snapshot is empty or no issuer matches, so OpenSSL reports X509_V_ERR_UNABLE_TO_GET_CRL and the handshake fails closed; the callback never throws and never logs

FLAG VALIDATION, all fail closed at startup with SRV_ERR: --mtls-crl-reload-interval negative; value 1..4 (minimum is 5, to prevent a hot stat loop); non-zero with an empty --mtls-crl-file; and on a build without OpenSSL 3.0+ (BoringSSL / LibreSSL / OpenSSL 1.1.x) the flag aborts startup rather than being silently ignored
change detection uses the (mtime, size) pair, not mtime alone. The (mtime, size) memo controls whether we RE-PARSE; it must NOT control whether we RE-WARN (challenger R-C4)

EXPIRY WARNINGS + PERSISTENT-FAILURE VISIBILITY (challenger R-C4, closes OQ-C1's real gap): on every tick the active snapshot's earliest nextUpdate is checked - SRV_WRN under 24h, SRV_ERR once passed ('all mTLS handshakes will fail'), each rate-limited to once per hour. ADDITIONALLY, a failed reload is re-logged at SRV_ERR once per hour for as long as the active snapshot is older than the on-disk file (NOT once per distinct (mtime,size), which would announce a permanently broken reload exactly once and then never again). Track consecutive_failures and last_success_unix; after 24h with no successful reload the message escalates and names the flag and the file

crl_reload_stop() (challenger R-C2) is a single std::atomic<bool> store and NOTHING else - no mutex, no condition_variable, no notify. The reload thread sleeps in 1-second increments and re-checks the flag. Rationale: server_http_context::stop() is reachable from the signal-delivery path (server.cpp:26-38) and condition_variable::notify_one locks, so it is no more async-signal-safe than pthread_join. The thread stays detached and touches only intentionally-leaked file-scope statics

DOCUMENTATION: the sentence 'A CRL is loaded once at startup; rotating the CRL requires restarting the server.' in the --mtls-crl-file help (common/arg.cpp:3545) is replaced, and the new --mtls-crl-reload-interval help states the last-known-good-on-failure policy explicitly
--mtls-crl-reload-interval is threaded through tools/server/tests/utils.py::ServerProcess and is usable from a --config YAML file with no common/config.cpp change
builds clean with and without OpenSSL (the no-OpenSSL harden_context #else path still fails closed) and with zero new warnings

SESSION RESUMPTION DISABLED (challenger R-C1, the real hole in F016): a resumed TLS session does NOT re-run chain verification - OpenSSL restores the stored peer cert and verify result - so a revoked client keeps connecting on new TCP connections for the ticket/session lifetime, defeating the entire point of a timely reload. When cfg.enabled && cfg.crl_reload_interval > 0, harden_context also calls SSL_CTX_set_session_cache_mode(c, SSL_SESS_CACHE_OFF), SSL_CTX_set_options(c, SSL_OP_NO_TICKET) and SSL_CTX_set_num_tickets(c, 0), with one SRV_INF explaining why. TEST: a client revoked by the reloaded CRL that reconnects presenting a previously-issued session ticket is REJECTED

SINGLE STARTUP PARSE (challenger B2-c): crl_parse_file is called EXACTLY ONCE at startup. load_crl_file is rewritten to take the already-parsed snapshot and only add it to the store plus set X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK|CRL_CHECK_ALL; the same snapshot object is published via crl_set. Design section 5.6's two separate parses (step 1 and step 2b) are a TOCTOU: a rotation between them can leave the store and the snapshot holding different files, or leave an EMPTY snapshot on a server that started 'successfully' and then fails every handshake. A parse failure at startup aborts, unchanged from F010a

CALLBACK ROBUSTNESS (challenger R-C5): crl_lookup_cb's whole body is wrapped in try{...}catch(...){ return nullptr; }; a NULL from sk_X509_CRL_new_null() returns NULL; a failed sk_X509_CRL_push X509_CRL_free's the CRL it just up-reffed (otherwise the reload leaks one CRL per handshake). Both nullptr and an empty stack produce fail-closed verification
the reload path never calls X509_STORE_set_flags or any other X509_STORE mutator (challenger R-C6); flags are set exactly once, by the startup add-to-store step

DOCUMENTATION (challenger R-C7): the --mtls-crl-reload-interval help states in one sentence that --mtls-client-ca-file is still loaded once at startup, so nobody infers general hot-reload of mTLS config; and it repeats design section 0's advice to prefer short-lived certificates when there is no real CRL distribution point

CRL FRESHNESS IS OBSERVABLE (challenger R-C4): server_mtls exposes crl_stats(uint64_t & reload_failures, int64_t & last_success_unix, int64_t & earliest_next_update). server-mtls.cpp and server-auth.cpp are in the same static lib (tools/server/CMakeLists.txt:38-54), so IF F015 ships, its emitter appends llamacpp_mtls_crl_reload_failures_total, llamacpp_mtls_crl_last_success_timestamp_seconds and llamacpp_mtls_crl_next_update_timestamp_seconds - three unlabelled series, no cardinality risk. If F015 does not ship, the hourly re-log stands alone and the flag help must say so
features.notes: Design complete, challenger review REQUIRED next (security_sensitive). docs/design/pr7-additional-hardening.md section 5 is the contract; open questions OQ-C1..OQ-C7 in section 5.10. Two architect decisions the challenger should attack hardest: (a) bad reload keeps the last-known-good CRL and logs SRV_ERR rather than aborting, justified in 5.4 on the grounds that aborting hands a DoS to anyone who can write the CRL file (OQ-C1); (b) the X509_STORE_set_lookup_crls mechanism in 5.3 rests on X509_STORE_CTX_init propagating the store's lookup_crls into the per-verification context and get_crl_delta preferring it over the store - confirm there is no path where the store-resident old CRL wins over the callback's new one, which would be a fail-open (OQ-C3). The startup add_crl safety net plus the 'revoked only in v2' test are the two guards against that assumption being wrong. CHALLENGER PASS COMPLETE (design section 7): BLOCKER B2 found - the 'X509_STORE_add_crl safety net' does not exist. There is one lookup_crls slot per store; the store-resident add_crl'd CRLs are reachable ONLY via the default X509_STORE_CTX_get1_crls, which the custom callback replaces, so they become inert. Answering OQ-C3 directly: OpenSSL does NOT consult both sources, and there is therefore NO path where the store-resident v1 CRL beats the callback's v2 CRL (no fail-open) - but neither is there a net, and a broken callback yields X509_V_ERR_UNABLE_TO_GET_CRL on every handshake, which is fail-CLOSED. The MECHANISM is sound; only the risk narrative was wrong. Also binding: R-C1 session-resumption bypass (the substantive security gap - a resumed session skips chain verification entirely, so revocation does not take effect until tickets expire), B2-b lookup_crls install assertion, B2-c single startup parse, R-C2 signal-safe stop, R-C3 drop the server-http.cpp call site, R-C4 persistent-failure visibility and CRL freshness gauges, R-C5 callback robustness. OQ-C1 resolved: last-known-good is CORRECT policy, but the alerting was NOT adequate and R-C4 fixes it. Verified: the OpenSSL 3.x lookup_crls signature is (const X509_STORE_CTX *, const X509_NAME *) per x509_vfy.h:271-273, and harden_context runs exactly once at startup (server-http.cpp:154) so the thread cannot be started twice.

Fixed by casting to (long long) and using %lld; both the OpenSSL and no-OpenSSL (build-nossl) configs now rebuild with zero new warnings. B2-c single startup parse confirmed: crl_parse_file is called exactly once in harden_context, the resulting snapshot is passed to load_crl_snapshot_to_store (add-to-store only, no re-parse) and separately published via crl_set for the reload thread - no TOCTOU between two independent parses.
